To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The hippocampus is involved in the retrieval and comparison of spatial and episodal details associated with a known environment; 2) The posterior hippocampus is involved with fine-grained spatial comparisons, while the anterior hippocampus is involved more in episodic comparisons; 3) The default mode network, including posterior cingulate, retrosplenial cortex, and medial prefrontal cortex, is involved in the comparison of spatial and/or episodic details associated a known environment.

fine-grained spatial judgments and episodic judgments both recruit the hippocampus, but in addition fine-grained spatial judgment recruit a region of the right hippocampus and episodic judgments recruit a region of left hippocampus, while fine-grained spatial and episodic judgments also recruit different sets of brain regions outside of the hippocampus.
